clinicalPearls: A diagnosis of exclusion characterised by severe, often disabling, unilateral or bilateral loin pain accompanied by haematuria in the absence of an identifiable structural, infective, or glomerular cause
Predominantly affects young to middle-aged women
Haematuria may be macroscopic or microscopic and is often intermittent; the pain is frequently out of proportion to objective findings
The condition is defined only after thorough exclusion of stones, tumour, infection, glomerular disease, clotting disorders, and vascular causes such as nutcracker syndrome
Renal biopsy may show non-specific findings such as C3 deposition or thickening of the glomerular basement membrane, but is mainly used to exclude other pathology
Management is challenging and centres on multidisciplinary chronic pain control; invasive and ablative procedures have unpredictable and often disappointing results
Careful psychological assessment and support are integral, without dismissing the pain as non-organic
reference.pathophysiology: The cause of loin pain-haematuria syndrome is poorly understood and probably heterogeneous. Proposed mechanisms include abnormalities of the glomerular basement membrane allowing red cells to escape into tubules, where they may form microcrystals or casts that provoke tubular obstruction and pain; intrarenal vascular or microvascular abnormalities; and abnormal pain processing or sensitisation. Because no single consistent lesion is found, the syndrome is best regarded as a clinical entity defined by its symptom complex once other renal and urological diseases have been rigorously excluded.
additionalInvestigations: Urinalysis, microscopy for dysmorphic red cells and casts, and culture
CT urography and ultrasound to exclude stones, tumour, and obstruction
Cystoscopy and, where indicated, ureteroscopy to localise bleeding and exclude urothelial lesions
Doppler or cross-sectional venous imaging to exclude nutcracker phenomenon
Coagulation screen and renal function tests
Renal biopsy to exclude glomerular disease when clinically warranted
redFlags: Features suggesting malignancy, such as a mass, weight loss, or persistent unexplained macroscopic haematuria
Signs of obstruction, infection, or sepsis requiring urgent intervention
New proteinuria or declining renal function pointing to an alternative diagnosis
reference.prognosis: The natural history is variable; some patients improve or remit over time, but many experience a chronic relapsing course with substantial impact on quality of life, and durable relief from invasive interventions is inconsistent.
pitfalls: Labelling a patient with the syndrome before adequately excluding treatable structural, glomerular, or vascular causes
Escalating to irreversible surgery such as nephrectomy or renal denervation with unpredictable benefit
Dismissing the pain as purely psychogenic and failing to provide multidisciplinary support
Overlooking nutcracker syndrome, which can mimic the presentation but is potentially treatable
management: Establish the diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out stones, tumour, infection, glomerular disease, coagulopathy and nutcracker phenomenon before committing to symptomatic treatment
Base management on multidisciplinary chronic-pain control with simple analgesia and neuropathic agents such as amitriptyline or gabapentinoids, limiting opioid escalation
Incorporate psychological support and pain-coping strategies given the central pain component and impaired quality of life
Consider interventional options such as nerve blocks or ureteric catheter analgesia in refractory pain, counselling that response is variable

Reserve ablative or surgical procedures such as renal denervation, ureterolysis, autotransplantation or nephrectomy for refractory disease, warning that durable relief is inconsistent and symptoms may recur or transfer to the other side
Monitor renal function and blood pressure and avoid repeated invasive investigation once the diagnosis is secure
Manage jointly through urology, nephrology and a specialist pain service, escalating for disabling pain or opioid dependence
